title: Central Bank keeps policy rate at 8.75% due to inflation rise - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) has decided to maintain the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 8.75%, citing the need to carefully assess evolving domestic and global economic conditions.

The Monetary Policy Board, at its meeting held yesterday (21), decided to keep the policy rate unchanged, while warning that renewed tensions in the Middle East have pushed up global commodity prices, particularly petroleum prices, creating risks for economic growth.

According to the CBSL’s latest Monetary Policy Review for July 2026, headline inflation increased to 6.8% year-on-year in June 2026, mainly due to higher domestic energy and food prices.

The Central Bank said inflation is expected to remain above the 5% target in the near term before gradually returning to the targeted level. Core inflation is also expected to rise and remain around the headline inflation target.

Although the recent increase in inflation has largely been driven by supply-side factors, the CBSL noted that domestic demand conditions have strengthened. However, it expects the monetary policy tightening introduced in May 2026 and other government measures to gradually moderate credit growth and demand pressures.

The Central Bank said external sector pressures caused by the Middle East conflict have eased to some extent, but uncertainty remains due to renewed geopolitical tensions.

Since April 2026, Sri Lanka’s external current account has recorded a deficit, mainly due to increased fuel import costs widening the trade deficit and a slowdown in tourism earnings.

Meanwhile, workers’ remittances have remained strong during 2026, while gross official reserves stood at USD 6.45 billion at the end of June 2026, including the swap facility from the People’s Bank of China.

The Sri Lankan rupee has also stabilised in recent weeks, reflecting the impact of policy measures implemented so far, the CBSL said.

The Central Bank said that it will continue monitoring domestic and global developments and is prepared to take appropriate measures to ensure inflation stabilises around the 5% target while supporting economic growth.

The next regular monetary policy review statement is scheduled to be released on September 30, 2026.

title: Three-wheeler plunges into Mohini Ella ravine, two killed - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Maskeliya, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - Two people were killed and two children were critically injured after a three-wheeler traveling from Nallathanniya towards Maskeliya plunged down a steep ravine near Mohini Ella, police said.

According to initial reports, the three-wheeler was carrying four passengers, including two elderly adults and two children, when the accident occurred.

The two elderly passengers died at the scene, while the two children sustained critical injuries and were admitted to hospital for emergency treatment.

title: Godzilla vs Kong actress Kaylee Hottle dies in crash at 18 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
BBC - US actress Kaylee Hottle, who starred in the Godzilla vs Kong movie series, has died in a car crash at age 18.

Hottle, who was deaf, portrayed a young orphan named Jia in the 2021 blockbuster, and reprised the role in 2024 sequel Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire.

Her father, Joshua Hottle, posted a video statement via Facebook, using American Sign Language to confirm details of her death.

Police officers in Frederick, Maryland, said "excessive speed" was believed to be a factor in the single-vehicle crash on Tuesday morning.

The Texas School for the Deaf, where Hottle had studied, also shared the news with "profound sadness".

"Our hearts are with Kaylee's family, friends, classmates, and everyone who knew and loved her during this incredibly difficult time," said a statement posted on Instagram.

It also called for everyone to respect the privacy of her family and to not speculate about the crash.

Warner Bros, which distributed the popular monster films, paid tribute to the actress alongside a photo of her in a post on X.

Frederick County Sheriff's Office said deputies were called to the scene of the crash in Ijamsville at about 02:50 local time.

Police said a 19-year-old driver was taken to hospital to be treated for "non life-threatening" injuries, while a second passenger declined help at the scene.

Hottle appeared in Godzilla vs Kong alongside Hollywood stars including Alexander Skarsgard, Millie Bobby Brown and Rebecca Hall.

Her role in the 2024 sequel earned her a Saturn Award nomination for best younger performer in a film.

title: Four-hour water cut in several Kandy areas today - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Mangala Pavithrani

Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has announced that water supply to several areas in Kandy will be temporarily suspended for four hours today (22) due to essential maintenance work at the Kandy Main Water Supply Project.

Accordingly, the water supply interruption will be in effect from 10.00 a.m. to 2.00 p.m.

The NWSDB said areas supplied by the Rajapihilla Service Reservoir will be affected, including Uduwawala, Polwatte Road, Glewatte, Wasgewatte, Uda and Palle Bokalawala, Piha Oyewatte, Ahasliyada, Kotuwewatte, Nagahamula Road, Thawalangoda, Balagolla, Hapugoda, Pattiyawatte, Rajapihilla, Moragahawela, Attaragama, Ulladupitiya Road, Poharabetenna Road and Attaragama Dekinda Road.

Areas under the Old Medawala Service Reservoir, including Kevumkohe Road, Gonigoda, Jayanthi Road, Gurukate, Palkumbura, Idamegama, Ambegama, Gorokgasanga Road, Elamalpatha, Kotuthenna, Pethiyagodawatta, Kaluwana, Bothota, Harankahatenna, Dodamthenna, Kumburegedara, Dembaralova, Thibbutta and Thalapellegoda Road, will also experience the disruption.

The water interruption will further affect areas supplied by the New Medawala Service Reservoir, including Batugoda, Ehelagashinna, Diddeniya, Owissa, Watagoda, Dombagammana, Hadeniya, Suriyakumbura, Ambaruppa, Harankahawa, Bokkawala, Walathenna and Pathirada.

The NWSDB said water supply will also be suspended in areas covered by the Galagedara Service Reservoir, including Galagedara, Webada, Boyagoda, Rambukkana Road, Poholiyadda Road and Kurunegala Road.

The Mawathagama Service Area, including Mawathagama, Barandana Road and Rambukkana Road, will also be affected during the maintenance period.

The NWSDB requested residents in the affected areas to store sufficient water in advance and make necessary arrangements until normal supply is restored.

title: Police urge vehicle rental firms to tighten security amid rising fraud - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - Police have urged vehicle rental companies to strengthen their security measures, warning that fraudsters are using fake identities, suspicious payment methods and deceptive tactics to obtain rental vehicles before disappearing without a trace.

Police said that rental operators should not hand over vehicles without thoroughly verifying the identity of customers, noting that a few extra minutes spent on verification could prevent the loss of a vehicle worth millions of rupees.

According to Police, rental companies should inspect original National Identity Cards (NICs) and driving licences, ensure the person collecting the vehicle matches the identification documents, and obtain a recent photograph or selfie for their records. They also recommend verifying the customer's permanent address through a recent utility bill or Grama Niladhari certificate and confirming that the provided mobile phone number is active through a live call or one-time password (OTP).

Police have also advised operators to strengthen technical security by installing reliable GPS tracking devices in every rental vehicle and ensuring they remain operational at all times. CCTV cameras should also be installed at vehicle collection and drop-off points to capture clear footage of customers.

In a bid to make suspects easier to trace, Police recommend avoiding cash transactions and accepting payments only through credit cards, debit cards or bank transfers linked to a Sri Lankan bank account in the customer's name.

Police further advised rental businesses to sign legally binding rental agreements, obtain verified guarantors for long-term rentals and clearly state that the vehicle cannot be driven by anyone other than the registered renter or subleased to a third party.

Highlighting several warning signs, Police said rental operators should be suspicious of customers who demand vehicles urgently while offering to pay more than the usual rental rate, present questionable identification documents, show unusual interest in the vehicle's GPS system or security features, or insist on collecting vehicles only at night.

Police urged vehicle rental businesses to remain vigilant, warning that organised fraudsters continue to exploit weak security procedures to steal vehicles, making strict verification and monitoring essential before every rental transaction.

title: State entities face heat over delayed annual reports and financial mismanagement - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya addressing the conference

Pic by Pradeep Pathirana

By Nishel Fernando

Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya this week rebuked ministries and state institutions over years-long delays in filing annual reports and financial statements, revealing that some audit reports remain pending after several years.

The Prime Minister highlighted the urgent need for sound management accounting and strict accountability within the public sector to support Sri Lanka’s ongoing economic recovery.

She emphasised that many government ministries and institutions have historically failed to adhere to basic accounting principles and oversight mechanisms.

“I regret to say that there are some institutions, some ministries, we are still looking at annual reports and audit statements from as far back as 2017, 2018, and 2019,” Prime Minister Amarasuriya said while addressing the CMA Sri Lanka International Management Accounting Conference 2026 in Colombo this week.

She noted that it is only now that the government is successfully pushing these institutions to bring their financial reporting up to current status.

“This has been a huge struggle that we have witnessed over the last one and a half years where many of these good financial practices or accounting principles have simply not been followed,” she noted, pointing out a systemic lack of accountability in the past.

These sentiments are strongly reflected in recent parliamentary records, which highlight ongoing discrepancies and severely delayed submissions. A review of the Papers Presented in the Parliament of Sri Lanka showcases instances where annual reports are submitted several years past their designated financial year.

For instance, recent Auditor General reports on the Janatha Estates Development Board revealed that financial statements and draft annual reports for 2021, 2022, and 2023 had not been presented to the Auditor General even by late 2024. Furthermore, oversight findings consistently indicate financial struggles alongside these administrative delays.

The corporate sector was assured that such lapses are no longer tolerated, with the Prime Minister declaring that “these accounting standards have to be followed, accounts have to be presented on time, they have to meet standards, and those that do not are held to account.”

Beyond basic financial reporting, the government is also pushing for broader transparency and long-term value creation through modern sustainability standards. The Prime Minister drew attention to the shifting global expectations around environmental and social responsibility, which are now being deeply integrated into corporate frameworks.

“This changing global landscape is reflected in the introduction of mandatory sustainability disclosure standards under SLFRS S1 and SLFRS S2 for leading listed companies,” Prime Minister Amarasuriya explained.

Detailing the strategic impact of these guidelines, she said: “While SLFRS S1 provides a framework for reporting sustainability-related risks and opportunities that may affect an organization’s financial performance, SLFRS S2 focuses specifically on climate-related risks and opportunities.”

Although these standards were initially targeted at leading listed companies, it was stressed that these sustainability and governance principles are equally relevant and necessary for the public sector. Effective public financial management depends on accurate and timely information that allows the government to plan strategically and utilize public resources efficiently.

title: Former State Minister’s son arrested over Rs. 20M robbery - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - The son of former State Minister Shanta Bandara has been arrested by the Colpetty Police in connection with the alleged robbery of Rs. 20 million belonging to a Chinese national.

Police said the 21-year-old suspect was taken into custody as part of an ongoing investigation into the incident, which allegedly took place on July 13.

Police said the robbery occurred while the Chinese national was transporting the cash in a vehicle.

Police have already arrested four other suspects in connection with the incident, all of whom have been remanded pending further investigations.

Police said that a grandson (19) of a prominent businessman is among those allegedly linked to the case.

The 21-year-old suspect is expected to be produced before court.

title: CIABOC begins probe on former Minister Akila Viraj - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Roshan Thushara

The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has launched an investigation into allegations that former United National Party (UNP) General Secretary Akila Viraj Kariyawasam committed an offence of corruption by recruiting employees to the Presidential Secretariat and deploying them for his personal and political activities.

As part of the ongoing investigation, Kariyawasam was summoned to appear before the Commission today (21) for further inquiries into the alleged use of Presidential Secretariat employees for political work.

However, CIABOC said that as of this afternoon, Kariyawasam had not appeared before the Commission and had not informed officials of any reason for his absence.

The investigation is being conducted under provisions of the Bribery Act relating to the misuse of public servants for private or political purposes, which constitutes an offence of corruption.

title: Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra detained by Delhi Police amid protest near PM residence
summary: Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were detained by the Delhi Police on Tuesday while leading a protest near Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s official residence at Lok Kalyan Marg, where Congress leaders were demanding accountability over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak and seeking the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

title: Pakistan steps in as US-Iran war widens and Hormuz shipping stalls
summary: Diplomatic efforts intensified on Tuesday to revive the collapsed interim agreement between Iran and the United States, even as both sides continued attacks for a 10th day of renewed fighting. Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni travelled to Pakistan, which has been trying to mediate between the two countries, but it was not immediately clear what fresh arrangement could emerge to end the war.

title: Crossings dominate market activity as ASPI extends decline - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Almas Equities Research

The Colombo Stock Exchange ended Tuesday's session on a mixed note, with the ASPI closing lower despite a strong start to the day, as renewed selling pressure erased early gains. The benchmark index climbed nearly 70 points within the first 15 minutes of trading, supported by buying interest in selected large-cap counters. However, the momentum gradually faded as profit-taking and continued selling pressure weighed on the broader market, leaving the ASPI to finish the session in negative territory.

Although market turnover rose sharply compared to the previous session, the improvement was largely driven by high-value crossing transactions rather than broad-based investor participation. Retail sentiment remained cautious, while institutional and value-oriented investors continued to execute strategic block trades. The ASPI also edged closer to the key 21,000-point level, reflecting the prevailing cautious mood among market participants.

The ASPI declined by 62.31 points, or 0.29%, to close at 21,145.73, while the S&P SL20 Index edged up by 1.79 points, or 0.03%, to settle at 5,945.01. Total market turnover amounted to LKR 3.27 Bn, with 38.52 Mn shares traded.

The Food Retailing sector emerged as the largest contributor to market turnover, generating LKR 2.32 Bn with 4.32 Mn shares traded. CARG.N dominated sector activity, recording LKR 2.32 Bn in turnover on 3.69 Mn shares traded. Crossing transactions accounted for LKR 2.49 Bn, representing a substantial 76% of total market turnover, with the largest crossing recorded in CARG.N amounting to LKR 2.26 Bn involving 3.59 Mn shares.

Market breadth remained weak, with 133 decliners outweighing 76 gainers, highlighting continued selling pressure despite selective buying interest in several large-cap counters. DIAL.N was the largest positive contributor to the ASPI, adding 9.81 points, followed by JKH.N, LION.N, SEMB.X, and SPEN.N. On the downside, CINS.N exerted the biggest drag on the index, reducing it by 22.56 points, while COMB.N, RICH.N, CARS.N, and HARI.N also weighed on overall market performance.

Among notable trades, CARG.N generated LKR 2.32 Bn in turnover on 3.69 Mn shares traded, while the counter edged up by 0.04% during the session. Despite the significant increase in turnover, the dominance of crossing transactions and weak market breadth suggest that broader investor sentiment remains cautious as participants await stronger earnings-driven catalysts.

title: Govt. has purchased over 1,900 metric tons of paddy since July - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - The government has purchased a total of 1,910 metric tons of paddy as of yesterday (20), Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said.

Speaking at the media briefing to announce Cabinet decisions today (21), the Minister said the Paddy Marketing Board (PMB) has spent Rs. 229.35 million on paddy purchases since the procurement programme commenced on July 13.

He said the government aims to purchase a total of 39,500 metric tons of paddy, with Rs. 6 billion allocated to the PMB for the programme.

In addition, a further Rs. 10 billion has been allocated under the ‘Odapana’ loan scheme to support the initiative.

Minister Jayatissa said the government had initially planned to open 143 paddy warehouses for the purchasing programme. However, as harvesting has not yet commenced in all areas, only 71 warehouses are currently in operation.

He noted that the 71 warehouses had purchased 1,910 metric tons of paddy by yesterday, with the PMB allocating Rs. 229.35 million for the procurement process.

title: My last days in Parliament: MP Archchuna - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - Referring to his political future, independent MP Ramanathan Archchuna today said he is currently spending his last days in Parliament.

"I will not be in Parliament for long. I will be in Parliament for two more weeks only," he told the House.

He said the case filed by Oshala Herath asking the Judiciary to remove me from Parliament will create a wrong impression that Sinhalese people do not want independent MPs.
